title: Adaptive Eligibility Harness for Enterprise Hosted API Requests — chat/streaming/toolcalls/structured
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: Build an adaptive eligibility harness that standardizes how enterprise feature requests for the Hosted API (chat, streaming, tool/function calls, structured outputs) are ingested, scored, and routed to the right intake lane. This will formalize signals, automate deterministic gating for SLAs/security, and produce clear decision artifacts for PM/Eng/Design reviews.

Scope: The harness will cover: (1) request schema and intake form validation; (2) signal extraction (sla requirement, data sensitivity, expected throughput, latency SLOs, legal/regulatory flags); (3) weighted scoring engine with configurable priorities for revenue, security, customer maturity, effort; (4) automated lane assignment (self-serve / low-touch / sales-assisted / enterprise program); (5) deterministic escalation rules to Security/Compliance or Dedicated/Private product tracks; (6) acceptance criteria for rollouts and a canary checklist for combined streaming+toolcalls+structured outputs.

Why now: Enterprise inbound volume for streaming+toolcalls has grown; current manual triage causes inconsistent routing, missed SLA terms, and delays in correctly flagging security/compliance work. This increases risk of under-provisioning Dedicated capacity or shipping insecure fallbacks.

Key decisions to capture here: scoring signal weights (default vs enterprise override), whether to require a minimal tech-readiness checklist before assigning to 'sales-assisted', and the fallback model policy (automated downgrade to CPU-hosted short-response path vs queue-with-notify).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form validates required signals (sla_class, data_sensitivity, estimated_rps, required_features) and rejects incomplete enterprise requests; 2) Scoring engine produces stable lane assignment for 95% of sample enterprise requests in historical dataset; 3) SLA/security flags automatically open tickets to Security when data_sensitivity >= medium and legal_region == EU; 4) Routing decisions link to an upgrade path (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) with suggested capacity estimate; 5) Console view exists showing top 10 pending enterprise requests and their computed priority score; 6) Playbook for PM/SE to handle manual overrides and to communicate fallback behavior to customers is published.
